title: A canvas notice can carry the way out
goal: When a key press cannot do what you asked, the line at the bottom of the canvas now says why and names what to do instead. You then have to go and find that command in a menu yourself, which is three steps for a thing the app has already worked out. The notice should be able to carry the way out as a button you can press, so the refusal and its answer are one move. It also has to stay a notice: it appears unprompted, so it must never steal the keyboard or sit there waiting to be dismissed.
notes:
Design review 2026-09-08. The runner who built Turn Into Picture asked for this in queue/audits/2026-09-08-turn-into-a-picture.json: "The pill still cannot be clicked. Offering the command as a button inside the refusal itself would be one step instead of three, but no notice pill in the app has an action in it yet, and adding the first one is a bigger change than this task. Say the word and it becomes its own task." This is that task.

It is a foundation change, so it needs the doc changed with it: docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 3 defines Canvas notice as a surface that "takes no input, has no close control". That sentence is what made the runner stop, and it was right to stop. Either the rule gains a narrow exception for a refusal offering its own way out, or this task answers that a notice must stay inert and the way out belongs somewhere else. Decide that first, in the audit, before building.
acceptance: The refusal you get from Delete or Command X over a marquee on a shape offers Turn Into Picture as something you can press, and pressing it does the same as the menu item including the question it asks first
A notice with an action still fades on its own like any other notice, and never takes the keyboard focus away from the canvas
A notice with no action looks and behaves exactly as it does today
The action is reachable from the keyboard for someone who does not use a pointer, and the audit says how
The rule for a notice that carries an action is written into the panels and surfaces vocabulary, since the current rule says a notice takes no input
A walk presses the action and proves the shape became a picture
